## Purpose

This SOP describes the calibration, field operation, and maintenance
of standalone handheld dissolved oxygen (DO) meters for in situ
measurement of dissolved oxygen concentration and percent saturation
in surface waters. Dissolved oxygen is a fundamental indicator of
water quality and aquatic habitat condition [@apha2012]. This SOP
covers both optical (luminescent) and electrochemical (polarographic
and galvanic) DO probes operated as standalone instruments, separate
from multiparameter sondes.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Handheld DO meters (e.g., YSI Pro20i, YSI ProSolo,
  Hach HQ40d with LDO probe, Extech DO600) used for in situ DO
  measurements at EA Program surface water field sites
- **Does not apply to:** DO measured by the Eureka Manta2 multiprobe
  (see [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd)); Winkler titration
  (laboratory method); BOD~5~ analysis (see
  [SOP-L306](../lab_sops/SOP-L306-bod5.qmd)); continuously deployed
  sondes
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve instrument selection; review QC data            |
| Trained Personnel | Calibrate and operate the meter per this SOP            |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **Barometric pressure correction:** Adjustment of the 100% saturation
  calibration point for the ambient atmospheric pressure; oxygen
  solubility decreases with decreasing pressure (increasing altitude);
  entered in mmHg or hPa at the time of calibration [@apha2012].
- **DO percent saturation (%sat):** The measured DO concentration
  expressed as a percentage of the equilibrium saturation concentration
  at the same temperature and pressure; 100% indicates equilibrium with
  the atmosphere; supersaturation (> 100%) indicates net photosynthesis;
  values well below 100% indicate high oxygen demand or poor reaeration
  [@apha2012].
- **Electrochemical (polarographic/galvanic) probe:** A DO sensor in
  which oxygen diffuses through a gas-permeable membrane and is reduced
  at the cathode, generating a current proportional to DO concentration;
  requires periodic membrane and electrolyte replacement and is flow-
  dependent (needs water movement past the membrane) [@apha2012].
- **KCl electrolyte:** The potassium chloride solution filling the
  electrode cavity of polarographic DO probes; must be replaced when
  the membrane is changed or when readings become erratic.
- **LDO (luminescent dissolved oxygen) probe:** An optical sensor that
  measures DO by the quenching of luminescence from a ruthenium-dye
  sensing element by oxygen molecules; requires no electrolyte or
  membrane, no warm-up time, and no stirring [@hach_hq40d].
- **Membrane (DO probe):** The gas-permeable Teflon or polyethylene
  film covering the electrode of an electrochemical DO probe; must be
  free of bubbles, tears, or debris; replace if damaged or if readings
  are erratic.
- **Sensing cap:** The replaceable luminescent element on an optical
  DO probe; replace when the cap expires (typically 1--2 years) or
  when readings become erratic [@ysi_pro20i].
- **Winkler titration:** The reference wet-chemical method for DO
  determination; used to verify DO meter accuracy and required for
  calibration validation in some regulatory programs [@apha2012].
- **Zero-oxygen calibration:** A secondary calibration point using
  an oxygen-free solution (sodium sulfite with cobalt chloride catalyst)
  to verify the zero response of the DO probe; recommended when expected
  DO values are below 2 mg/L.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Measuring DO requires placing the probe in or near
  water. Slip, fall, and drowning hazards apply. Work in pairs at
  stream sites.
- **Chemical:** Polarographic DO probes use KCl electrolyte solution,
  a mild irritant. Sodium sulfite (used for zero-oxygen calibration)
  is a mild irritant and reducing agent.
- **Biological:** Water may contain pathogens. Avoid ingestion; wash
  hands after field work.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (especially for impaired waters)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## Instrument Types

### Optical (Luminescent) DO Probes

Optical probes (e.g., Hach HQ40d with LDO101 probe, YSI ProSolo ODO)
measure DO by detecting luminescence quenching. They require no
electrolyte, no warm-up time, no stirring, and no membrane replacement
[@hach_hq40d].

| Advantage                         | Limitation                              |
|:----------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|
| No membrane or electrolyte        | Higher initial cost                     |
| No stirring required              | Sensing cap has finite lifespan (1--2 yr) |
| Fast stabilization                |                                         |
| Lower maintenance                 |                                         |

### Electrochemical (Polarographic / Galvanic) DO Probes

Electrochemical probes (e.g., YSI Pro20i) measure DO through an
oxygen-permeable membrane [@ysi_pro20i].

| Advantage                         | Limitation                              |
|:----------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|
| Lower initial cost                | Requires membrane and electrolyte replacement |
| Well-established method           | Needs 5--15 min warm-up                 |
| Widely available                  | Flow-dependent (stirring or moving water needed) |


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Handheld DO meter with probe          | Fully charged; confirm calibration supplies |
| Water-saturated air calibration chamber | Wet sponge in probe storage cap       |
| Barometric pressure reference         | Built into some meters; otherwise Kestrel or phone app |
| Spare membranes and electrolyte       | For electrochemical probes              |
| Spare sensing cap                     | For optical probes; replace when expired or erratic |
| Thermometer (for verification)        | Most DO probes include temperature sensor |
| DI water (squeeze bottle)             | For rinsing the probe                    |
| Lint-free wipes                       | For drying the probe before calibration  |
| Field notebook                        | Per [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd) |
| Spare batteries                       | Matched to meter model                   |


## Procedure

### Calibration

Calibrate the DO meter before each field day using the
**water-saturated air** method.

**Water-saturated air calibration:**

1. Ensure the calibration chamber (probe storage cap with damp sponge)
   is moist but not dripping; the probe tip must not touch the sponge.
2. Turn on the meter. Allow electrochemical probes to warm up for
   5--15 minutes (see instrument manual) [@ysi_pro20i].
3. Enter the current barometric pressure (mmHg or hPa). Verify the
   displayed value against a Kestrel or weather station.
4. Place the probe in the calibration chamber; wait for the reading to
   stabilize (1--3 min for optical; 5--10 min for electrochemical).
5. Press **Cal** per the instrument prompts; the meter sets 100%
   saturation at the current temperature and pressure.
6. Record in the field notebook: calibration date, time, barometric
   pressure, temperature, and whether calibration was accepted.

**Zero-oxygen calibration (optional -- low-DO environments):**

1. Dissolve excess sodium sulfite in DI water with a pinch of cobalt
   chloride catalyst.
2. Immerse the probe and wait for the reading to stabilize.
3. Calibrate the zero point per meter instructions.

### Field Measurement

1. Immerse the probe to mid-depth at the sampling location. For
   electrochemical probes, maintain a minimum flow of 0.3 m/s past
   the membrane (gently move the probe in still water). Optical probes
   do not require flow [@hach_hq40d].
2. Wait for the reading to stabilize.
3. Record in the field notebook:
   - DO concentration (mg/L) and percent saturation (%)
   - Water temperature (°C) as reported by the probe
   - Date, time, sample ID, and measurement depth
   - Flow conditions (riffle, pool, still water with manual stirring)
4. For depth profiles, lower the probe in 0.5 or 1.0 m increments and
   allow stabilization at each depth.

### Post-Field Care

1. Rinse the probe with DI water after each use.
2. For electrochemical probes, check the membrane for tears, bubbles,
   or deposits; replace membrane and electrolyte if damaged
   [@ysi_pro20i].
3. For optical probes, gently wipe the sensing cap with a soft, damp
   cloth if biofouling is visible; do not use solvents.
4. Store the probe in the calibration chamber with a moist sponge
   (not submerged).
5. Turn off the meter; remove batteries if storing for more than one
   month.


## Data Interpretation

DO concentrations are influenced by temperature, atmospheric pressure,
salinity, photosynthesis, respiration, and reaeration [@apha2012].

| DO (mg/L) | Condition                              |
|:----------|:---------------------------------------|
| > 8       | Well-oxygenated; suitable for most aquatic life |
| 5--8      | Adequate for many species; marginal for cold-water fish |
| 2--5      | Stressful for most fish; hypoxic conditions |
| < 2       | Severe hypoxia; lethal to most aquatic organisms |


## Quality Control

- Calibrate at the start of each field day.
- At the end of the field day, check calibration by returning the probe
  to the water-saturated air chamber; reading must be within ±2% of
  100% saturation. If drift exceeds 5%, note it and recalibrate.
- When possible, verify against a second DO meter or the Eureka Manta2;
  readings should agree within ±0.5 mg/L.
- For long field days (> 6 hours), perform a mid-day calibration check.
- Record all QC results in the field notebook [@apha2012].

## Training Record

Before using DO meters independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate a complete water-saturated air calibration
3. Perform supervised DO measurements at one field site
4. Demonstrate membrane inspection and replacement (electrochemical
   probes) or sensing cap inspection (optical probes)
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
